name: Zephyrex
manufacturer: Shelf lab — attributed to a synthesist known only as Caraway
description: Zephyrex is an unlicensed street formulation that decouples cognitive performance from the physiological stress response — allowing the user to think clearly and effectively even under conditions of extreme fear, threat, or emotional overwhelm. It doesn't eliminate the stress response, but it builds a firewall between the body's alarm systems and the executive cognitive functions, keeping the mind clear while the heart races. Originally developed on the Shelf for people who need to think in genuinely dangerous situations.
effects: Cognitive performance maintained under extreme stress or fear
Decoupling of emotional arousal from executive function
Sustained decision-making quality in high-threat environments
Maintained working memory capacity during crisis
side_effects: Stress responses continue physically while cognitively masked — physiological damage accumulates unnoticed
Emotional unreality — situations that should feel dangerous don't register as such
Post-dose cortisol dump: crash involves all the stress response that was queued but not processed
Impaired risk-perception — users may make cognitively sound but contextually reckless decisions
Dependency: without it, users in stressful situations experience acute cognitive shutdown
Unknown long-term cardiovascular effects from chronic stress-response/cognition decoupling
cultural_context: Zephyrex was born on the Shelf for Shelf problems. When your job is debt-running through gang territory, negotiating with armed creditors, or surviving a housing seizure operation, the ability to think clearly under existential threat is not a performance optimization — it's survival. Caraway, the anonymous chemist behind the original formula, has achieved near-mythological status in Tier 1 communities. The drug has begun seeping upward: Tier 2-3 workers in high-stress, high-stakes jobs are discovering it, and there are rumors that certain military contractors are interested. The Shelf resents this appropriation, viewing Zephyrex as one of the few things they made for themselves.
story_hooks: Caraway — the Shelf chemist behind Zephyrex — has been found dead, and the formula has gone with them. Multiple parties are hunting for anyone who might have a copy: Lazarus wants to patent it, a Shelf gang wants to monopolize production, and someone wants it buried because a cleaner version is already in military development.

A Tier 3 corporate negotiator started using Zephyrex for high-stakes contract talks and now can't function in any stressful situation without it — her dependency is invisible to her colleagues because she performs perfectly, but she's slowly losing the ability to emotionally process the consequences of the decisions she makes.

A law enforcement unit has discovered that a crew of Shelf runners they've been chasing uses Zephyrex operationally — every time they corner them, the crew makes calm, coordinated decisions under fire that should be impossible. Someone needs to understand what they're dealing with before the next raid.
